# Dema Testing and Quality Matrix

This repo uses native Node.js tests and CLI smoke checks. The goal is behavior coverage: every public safety boundary should have a replayable local check.

## Commands

Run the full local gate:

```bash
npm test
npm run coverage
npm run check
npm run llm:guidance
npm run release:readiness
npm run gtm:readiness
npm run urp:discovery
npm run proof:room
npm run pre-push:seal
npm run layer-a5:prep
git diff --check
```

`npm run coverage` is a native Node coverage report and harness-failure check.
It enforces the repo coverage floor with Node's native threshold flags:
95% lines, 84% branches, and 95% functions.

Run one test file:

```bash
node --test tests/status.test.js
```

Run one test name pattern:

```bash
node --test --test-name-pattern="bounded diagnostic" tests/status.test.js
```

That is why one intermittent failure stayed unidentified across three slices: it was not merely lost to filtered output, it was deleted by design. Failing runs are now preserved and their path disclosed (`[G8 LOG] preserved failing run log: …`); green runs still clean up, which is the whole point of `--temp-log`. Both tests strip `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT` before spawning, because a nested `node --test` otherwise inherits the runner's reporter shape and emits no plain TAP, which the freshness gate correctly refuses. CL-14: an over-request clamped at derivation surfaces here as a refusal, never a silent widening. CL-15: a missing hash function is UNVERIFIABLE and a contract typo never silently downgrades to v0.1. 15 tests. DOCTOR-PREVIEW-RESTING-STATE adds a fourth predicate status `expected`: when no runtime is bridged at all (`status.adapter.available === false`, the `legacy-shellout-unavailable` payload) the three readiness predicates render `⏸` with a `note` instead of `❌` with a `Fix`, because those values are what a preview-only install reports by construction. Fail-closed on the signal exactly as `gatewayProbe` is on `reachable`: only an explicit `false` softens, and an absent `adapter` field (every gateway-http payload) never does. **Regression guards transport the attack** — a *bridged* runtime (`adapter.available === true`) reporting the same false values keeps `status=fail`, keeps its fix, still prints `❌` and still reads `Verdict: blocked`, so the softening cannot launder a real outage. The display softening is deliberately NOT paired with an exit-code change: `doctorState()` exports typed machine dimensions (`operational` / `preview_environment_valid` / `repair_required` / `reason`) and `operational` is the exit authority, so an unbridged node still exits non-zero. An invariant test binds `doctorState().operational === (doctorVerdict() === "ready and consent-gated")` across every fixture, closing a pre-existing case where a warn-only state printed `Verdict: blocked` while the process exited 0. |

The dashboard embedding addresses three concerns of distinct kinds — **security:** `</script>` script-element breakout prevention (exactly one legitimate closing tag; payload breakout escaped via `<`); **document integrity:** `String.replace` replacement-string corruption prevention (`$'`/`` $` ``/`$$` preserved literally via callback replacement; `$&` inert because `&` is escaped); **compatibility:** U+2028/U+2029 normalized to escaped form (legal unescaped since ES2019 — portability/older-tool hardening, not a modern-syntax fix). Source assertions: dashboard imports/uses `htmlSafeJson(statusPayload)`, no raw `JSON.stringify(statusPayload)`, callback `</body>` replacement. Helper fails closed with an explicit `TypeError` on top-level values `JSON.stringify` cannot serialize (`undefined`/function/symbol) rather than crashing or emitting non-JSON `undefined` — native `JSON.stringify` failures (BigInt, cyclic) still throw their own errors, outside this guard. 16 tests. |

| `tests/arabic-canonical-name.test.js`                   | ARABIC-NAME-GUARD + ARABIC-LIGATURE-GUARD-1A (TASK-031). Scans every tracked `*.md`/`*.js`/`*.mjs`/`*.ts`/`*.tsx`/`*.json` file for two classes of machine-mangled Arabic, both built from code points so the guard cannot flag its own source. (1) **Name guard** — BIZRA is `البذرة` (the seed, with thaal); the zaay spelling is a different word carrying none of the founding metaphor, and it entered a bilingual investor document three times before this gate existed. Asserts the canonical spelling is present in `packages/core/src/canon-glossary.js` so the guard has a referent. (2) **Ligature guard** — a bare alef immediately followed by a hamza-carrying alef (`ا` + `آأإ`), which cannot occur inside a valid Arabic word. That pattern is the signature of a lam-alef presentation form (`ﻹ`) decomposed back to base characters in the wrong order, which is what PDF text extraction does — and the root canon lives in `docs/root-canon/source/*.pdf`. Measured 2026-07-31: the canon tagline had reached an open PR opening U+0627 U+0625 U+0644 where canon opens U+0627 U+0644 U+0625 (`الإنسانية`) — the corrupted form is named by code point here, never rendered, because this row is itself scanned by the guard, 4 instances across the EN and AR sections of `docs/gtm/AUG2_OPERATION_FIRST_WITNESS.md`. `npm run eval:layer1` had reported that exact file `PUBLIC_SAFE` score 1 — Layer-1, the claim register, the claim-corpus gate and the no-overclaim scanner are all blind to orthography, so nothing else was looking. Zero false positives across 2,199 tracked files; the adjacent canon line `كل إنسان عقدة` is correct and must not flag, because the space prevents the ligature from forming. 3 tests total. |

Observes which BASES belong to this node — this host and any attached companion device — and how much of its own storage it cannot reach. **MEASURED DEFECT this pins (NBC-01)**: reachability computed per DISK reported a 1024 GB drive as fully reachable because a 2 GB partition on it was mounted, hiding a 1020 GB unmounted partition and contradicting `lsblk`; reachability is now partition-level and dark capacity is attributable to named partitions. NBC-03 proves a cabled device is surfaced as a base but `enrolled=false` — presence is never enrolment. NBC-05 re-derives every total so a hand-edited summary cannot hide dark capacity; NBC-08 (PR #458 review catch) extends the same law to the ENVELOPE-level summaries — `dark_capacity_gb`, `base_count`, `attached_not_enrolled` each re-derive, so tampering the headline fails with a named reason. Gatherer uses plain `/proc` and `/sys` reads with no child process (this host lacks `awk` and a working `cc`) and opens no device content. 8 tests. No pairing, no actuator, no mutation. |

The command computes the verdict INSIDE the emit path — an envelope whose totals do not re-derive from its own rows is refused with exit 1, never printed. A deterministic **denoising-convergence** kernel over a refinement trajectory (`drafts`): each step's `noise_score` (count of speculation/overclaim markers, fixed `DIFFUSION_NOISE_MARKERS` lexicon, incl. autonomy-overclaim phrases) must be non-increasing toward an evidence-bound zero-noise claim. `buildDiffusionRefinement`/`scoreDraftNoise`/`verifyDiffusionRefinement`. Statuses: `CONVERGED` (zero-noise + evidence), `DENOISED_UNEVIDENCED` (zero-noise, no evidence — honest), `REFINING` (still noisy), `DIVERGED` (noise increased). **NOT a neural diffusion model / learned sampling / stochastic / generative** — `neural_diffusion:false`, `learned_sampling:false`; verify fails closed on either overclaim. Content-addressed `draft_hash`/`convergence_hash`; **verify RE-DERIVES** per-step noise, `diverged_at_step`, `convergence_status`, `recommendation`, `final_noise_score`, and the attestation prose so a recomputed-hash laundering (DIVERGED→CONVERGED) is caught. Fail-closed: `drafts_empty`/`drafts_must_be_array`/`draft_malformed`; deep-frozen; purity test; all-false boundary. No model/network/text-generation/signing/mint/federation. Markers match on **word boundaries**, not bare substrings — `(?<!\w)..(?!\w)`, **`\w` only: the hyphen is a prose separator, NOT an identifier character**. "speak"/"peaked" do not score `peak`, "mighty" does not score `might`, "perfectly" does not score `perfect`; hyphenated compounds carrying a real marker — "might-be", "perfect-world", "semi-perfect" — DO still score (test 18). Underscore identifiers (`peak_phase`) stay exempt for free because `_` is a word character, and lexicon entries that themselves contain a hyphen still match as whole markers since each pattern is built from the entry verbatim. An earlier form used `(?<![\w-])..(?![\w-])`, borrowing the identifier-safety idiom from `scripts/review/no-overclaim.mjs`; that gate scans **source**, where `-` genuinely binds identifiers, while this kernel scores **prose**, where it does not — the borrow silently zeroed ordinary compounds, a false NEGATIVE on the predicate behind `CONVERGED`/`ACCEPT_CONVERGED` and strictly worse than the false positive it replaced. Accepted cost: a hyphenated command name like `peak-self-loop` scores 1 — deliberate, since **zero** hyphenated tokens in `dema --help` contain a marker segment (re-measured against the live lexicon; the kernel comment's "241" is one tokenizer's denominator — the numerator, 0, is what the argument rests on and is tokenizer-independent), so an identifier allowlist would exist for no documented command while prose stayed broken. Test 17 also asserts every marker still matches itself standalone so the fix cannot silently disarm the lexicon. |

|`tests/canonical-receipt.test.js` | [MEASURED] [LOCAL_ONLY] RECEIPT-CHAIN-1A canonical signed prev_hash receipt ledger kernel (`packages/receipts/src/canonical-receipt.js`). The trustless proof spine — closes the disk-verified gap that `~/.dema/receipts`is a flat bag (0 receipts carry`prev_hash`). `buildCanonicalReceipt({canonicalBody, prevHash, truthLabel, whatProves, whatDoesNotProve, consent, demaHome, now})`(pure-with-key-load, NO disk write — that is 1B) signs a content-addressed receipt chained to`prevHash`(null=genesis);`verifyCanonicalChain({entries, pubkeyPem})` (pure) walks the chain with ZERO trust — first step toward "Node2 verifies Node1". Schema:`bizra.dema.canonical_receipt.v0.1`. Body: `{schema, prev_hash, body_hash, canonical_body, truth_label, what_this_proves, what_this_does_not_prove, operator_public_key_fingerprint, created_at_iso}`+`receipt_id`(sha256 of body) +`receipt_signature_b64`. 10 tests. Authority = ONLY the external pubkey (embedded fingerprint never trusted — verdict-receipt REJECT-4 invariant). Verifier REJECTS: `entries_empty`·`external_pubkey_required`·`receipt_schema_mismatch`·`genesis_prev_hash_not_null`·`prev_hash_mismatch`(missing/wrong link on non-genesis)·`receipt_id_mismatch`(non-canonical body drift)·`body_hash_mismatch`(tampered content)·`signature_invalid`(wrong external key AND attacker-re-signed-with-key-B-verified-with-key-A). Builder fail-closed: `consent_required`/`created_at_iso_required`(no wall-clock)/`truth_label_invalid`/`what_this_proves_required`/`what_this_does_not_prove_required`/`prev_hash_invalid`/`no_authorship_key`. Deterministic; no PRIVATE KEY material. SCOPE 1A: kernel only — no `~/.dema/receipts`write (1B), no token/PoI/economy/federation. **CRYPTO-AGILITY-1A (v0.2):** v0.1 emitted `receipt_signature_b64` with ed25519 IMPLICIT, and no receipt anywhere in the tree declared its own algorithm — the exact condition `CRYPTO_ALGORITHM_UNDECLARED` exists to catch, with nothing producing it. v0.2 = v0.1 + `sig_alg` INSIDE the signed body, so `receipt_id` and the signature both commit to it (CA-01 proves the binding by stripping the field and showing the id changes — a field carried beside the body declares nothing). `buildCanonicalReceiptV0_2` is additive; `buildCanonicalReceipt` still emits v0.1, so no producer changes version underneath its callers, and CA-06 pins that dispatch is per entry (a v0.1 genesis chains to a v0.2 child). CA-03 is the negative control and AC#3: a v0.2 receipt whose `sig_alg` was stripped and resealed is refused `crypto_policy:CRYPTO_ALGORITHM_UNDECLARED` — this is `evaluateSignaturePolicy`'s FIRST production caller, on the verification path, after it shipped fully built with zero callers. CA-04: a body declaring `ML-DSA-65` over a signature this build verified with ed25519 is refused `DOWNGRADE_ATTACK_DETECTED` — a declaration nobody checks is decoration. CA-05: a v0.1 receipt carrying `sig_alg` is refused, because widening the older contract is how a version bump becomes a way to smuggle fields. CA-07: the authority-succession verifier enforces the identical rule, because both verifiers share one `checkEntryStructure` — two copies would drift into one verifier accepting a chain the other refuses. CA-08 pins `QSAFE_CUTOVER_AT === null`: no cutover is declared, so the hybrid branch is unreachable and this slice changes nothing at any future date; setting a date turns CA-08 red on purpose, because the policy call must first move to after the signature check or it would read an assumed `classicalValid` instead of a measured one. 23 tests. Mutation-controlled in an isolated clone (23/0 pristine): allowing v0.1 to widen → 1 red, accepting any declared algorithm → 1 red, never consulting the policy → 2 red, carrying `sig_alg` beside the body instead of inside it → 3 red. |

It authorizes nothing whose purpose is to change the world so the world agrees with the record — **it may finish recording the already-authorized result; it may not manufacture a world that matches the record.** **The slice is not "add resume":** resume already existed (`evidenceTailPhases` covers `LEDGER_COMMITTED`/`ANCHORED`/`RESOLVED`, and the ledger and anchor appenders are already idempotent). | `tests/c4d-cross-process-ownership-fencing.test.js`     | C4D-01…19 cross-process ownership and stale-worker fencing (Gate C, C4 step D). **LOCAL SINGLE-NODE ONLY** — this proves nothing about cross-host ownership, distributed consensus, network leases, leader election, federation, or a hostile root; the target is concurrent Node processes on one Node0 Linux host. **Durable event arbitration is not actuator fencing.** The transaction journal was already compare-and-append safe, so two racing workers produce exactly one durable event — that protects HISTORY, not the WORLD. The production route crossed the effect boundary in `applyPreparedMechanicalClosure` BEFORE the loser discovered it lost the append race, so both processes could rename the same path while the journal stayed perfectly truthful about only one of them. The corridor's only prior "lease" was `created_at_iso + time_budget_hours → lease_expired`, carrying no worker identity, process birth, or ownership token. **One transaction → one live local process owner → one current fencing token → every mutation proves that token immediately before acting.** **A clock cannot revoke a live owner:** a paused-but-living process keeps ownership, because otherwise it could wake after a takeover and both would touch the world; takeover is lawful only against a predecessor proven not to be the same live process. **PID alone is never sufficient.** `authorship-key-store.js` had already shipped the liveness-not-wall-clock law at CP5, and its primitives are reused rather than reinvented — O_EXCL + NO_FOLLOW, EPERM-means-alive/ESRCH-means-dead, unreadable-is-UNKNOWN, and a read-only inspector that never creates, refreshes or deletes. What that lease does not survive is PID reuse: a bare `process.kill(pid, 0)` reports "alive" for a recycled PID belonging to an unrelated process. Ownership here binds pid + `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 (start time) + hashed `boot_id`, so a recycled PID reads as a DEAD predecessor (C4D-04) and a prior-boot tuple cannot masquerade as live after reboot (C4D-04b). `/proc` parsing splits at the LAST `)` because the comm field may itself contain spaces and parentheses. **Unreadable identity fails closed** — `OWNERSHIP_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE`, `requires_human: true`, no takeover (C4D-05); an unreadable process is never guessed dead. The claim is an exact closed 12-key set of primitives under canonical-json.v1 with a body-bound `claim_hash` the verifier RE-DERIVES rather than trusts (a forged hash is refused), which is what structurally keeps raw command lines, environment, secrets, stacks and operator paths out of ownership evidence (C4D-18). Current ownership is a monotonic generation pointer published with the journal's own private-temp → fsync → hard-link → dir-fsync law, so exactly one of N competing takers wins generation N+1 and every loser replays the winner; nothing is ever overwritten or deleted, so predecessor claims survive as immutable history with an exact `predecessor_claim_hash` chain (C4D-06). **The fence re-reads the current owner FROM DISK on every mutation** — a token checked against cached state proves nothing about who owns the transaction right now. One guard at `appendDurableClosurePhase` covers all nine durable append sites (intent, applied, verified, sealed, and every rollback phase) rather than nine guards that rot when a tenth is added; the effect boundary revalidates separately because that is the last instant at which refusing is still free. A stale token returns `STALE_OWNER_FENCED` with `mutation_performed: false`, `event_appended: false`, `effect_retry_forbidden: true`, and `requires_human: false` when a valid newer owner exists — the stale worker may OBSERVE the winner, never replace, release, or write under it (C4D-07/08/09, C4D-14). Read-only replay and intent resolution stay ownership-free, and separate transactions never contend (C4D-16, no global lock). **Measured, and why the first shape was insufficient:** two real spawned processes both reported `ACQUIRED` because the winner exited the instant it acquired and a sibling then lawfully succeeded its dead claim — correct behaviour against an artificial scenario, since a production owner holds ownership across the effect. The racers now hold until released, which makes the test measure "at most one LIVE owner". More importantly, mutation testing showed the call-graph grep proved the fence was CALLED but not that its verdict was OBEYED: neutering the effect-boundary check and the acquisition check both left the isolated suite green. C4D-P1/P2 in `c4b2a-mechanical-rollback-wiring.test.js` therefore drive the real `runTransactionalMechanicalClosure` and assert on the world — a live foreign owner must produce an `ownership_held` refusal with `effect.apply` call count zero and the source file unrenamed, and a mid-flight takeover (seeded from the `manifest()` call that falls between acquisition and the boundary) must fence the effect. Chasing the surviving mutation also exposed a latent hazard: the chokepoint's `fencingToken !== null` convention means a null token silently disables the fence, so the production route now states its requirement explicitly instead of inheriting the permissive default. **A corpse cannot hold the world's lock (C4D-04c):** a process killed with SIGKILL stays in the table as a ZOMBIE until its parent reaps it — `/proc/<pid>/stat` still exists and its start time is unchanged, so pid + start + boot alone report the killed owner as ALIVE and refuse the very recovery that is supposed to succeed. Whether that window is observed depends on how quickly the parent waits, which is precisely the shape of an intermittent failure: before this check, 2 of 5 `npm run check` runs failed, one of them on `CCB-15: production CLI recovers a SIGKILL after no-replace target publication`; after it, 5 of 5 pass and the standalone suite was 6/6 either way. Process state is therefore read alongside start time and `Z`/`X`/`x` classify as DEAD; the state is carried on the probe for the liveness decision only and can never reach persisted evidence, because `buildClaim` picks the twelve claim keys explicitly. **The fence must also answer "for exactly WHICH transaction?" (C4D-BIND-01…09):** the first wiring passed `authority.prepared_intent_hash` as the claim's `transaction_hash`. C2 treats those as two different facts — the descriptor BODY contains `prepared_intent_hash` among other fields and `transaction_hash` is the hash OF that body, and `deriveRollbackBindingContext` carries both separately — so the claim asserted "owner of this prepared intent" while its schema said "owner of this exact C2 transaction", and one prepared intent can belong to more than one descriptor. The transaction-directory path made an immediate cross-transaction double effect unlikely, so this was a cryptographic misbinding rather than a demonstrated actuator failure; it is nonetheless blocking, because an ownership receipt that cannot prove which descriptor it belongs to proves nothing. `readVerifiedTransactionHash()` now re-reads `transaction.json` from disk, replays the chain, and returns the descriptor hash only after the SAME checks the rollback path uses — the descriptor-integrity half of `deriveRollbackBindingContext` was extracted into `verifyDescriptorAgainstChain()` so both callers share one verifier rather than a second weaker copy. `transaction_id` and `transaction_hash` are revalidated at acquisition, idempotent reacquisition and takeover (all reach the mismatch check before any branch), and the fence carries `expectedTransactionHash` through every durable append and the effect boundary. **Release is characterised, not changed (C4D-REL):** `releaseClosureOwnership()` exists but production never calls it, so the retirement path is death plus dead-owner takeover — proven safe by driving a real closure to terminal, seeding a dead unreleased owner at the next generation, and showing a successor performs terminal replay with the effect count unchanged and the durable head unmoved: ownership generations may advance while authority does not, so an unreleased dead claim never becomes a permanent lock. **Binding must hold at MUTATION time, not acquisition time (C4D-TOCTOU-01/03/07):** the first correction verified C2 once and carried the hash in memory, which proves "the current owner matches the transaction I checked earlier" — not "…matches the transaction that exists on disk at the instant I touch reality." Between those moments a descriptor or chain can be corrupted, replaced by an accidental competing writer, or drift in a fixture, and a cached hash would still agree with the owner claim while the authority beneath it had changed. `validateCurrentC2Ownership()` therefore re-derives the hash from disk through the shared verifier before every durable append and before the effect; no caller may thread a cached hash to a mutation boundary, and the call-graph test asserts that. The seam is `effect.manifest()`, which runs after acquisition and before the boundary, so tampering there lands inside the real window: a corrupted descriptor yields `transaction_binding_unverifiable` with `effect.apply` count zero and the source file unrenamed, a corrupted event chain appends nothing, and an untampered closure still runs green. **Not constructible, and said plainly:** the specified "different but well-formed descriptor" case has no reachable state, because C2 binds the descriptor hash into every event of the chain — swapping the descriptor always presents as unverifiable rather than as a clean mismatch, and the mismatch branch is exercised directly by C4D-BIND-06 instead. **Owned closure tail:** the opaque capability now spans rollback restoration, verification-failure undo, canonical ledger append, `LEDGER_COMMITTED`, anchor publication, `ANCHORED`, `COMPLETE` event construction, and `RESOLVED`; every mutation re-derives C2 ownership from disk at its boundary. Terminal `COMPLETE` recovery acquires a newer capability before restoring a missing `RESOLVED`, while separately consented `STOP` remains outside the COMPLETE capability. TAIL-15 drives two real processes against one post-ledger transaction and requires one durable winner, one explicitly fenced loser, one receipt, and one ordered C2 tail. The owned-tail matrix applies 11 faithful syntax-valid mutations (R1…R11), each matching its anchor exactly once and producing a mutant that still parses. Measured on these bytes: all 11 are caught BEHAVIOURALLY — every control turns red a test that executes the production route, never one that only scans source text. R4/R5/R6 drive the real CLI composition through `C4D-TAIL-05d`/`05e`/`05f` (takeover seeded before `LEDGER_COMMITTED`, before anchor publication, and after it); the `C4D-TAIL-05c` and `06b` source scans stay as defense-in-depth and qualify nothing on their own. R11 is caught by `C4D-TAIL-14`, which spawns the real `dema mission corridor stop` against an isolated `DEMA_HOME`: an independently consented STOP seals exactly one `STOPPED` event and terminates the corridor while acquiring no ownership claim, appending no C2 phase, and creating no canonical receipt and no anchor. All sixteen TAIL properties map to an executable behavioural test; none rests on source inspection alone. **Deployment constraint:** `C4D_WORKER_LIFECYCLE = ONE_SHOT_PROCESS_PER_TRANSACTION`, because ownership retires through process death and takeover while release stays unwired; a supervisor may spawn one-shot closure workers but must not run several closure transactions inside one long-lived worker. The earlier 16 controls cover the ownership module and pre-tail wiring, including wall-clock revocation, cached-state trust, overwrite publication, zombie handling, and the original transaction misbinding. The owned-tail 11-control matrix covers the remaining production tail and the STOP exclusion. 28 tests here; rollback and direct-adapter probes remain in C4B2A. |

Every new public surface should add or update tests for:

1. schema tag,
2. human output,
3. JSON output when available,
4. safe default,
5. non-execution boundary,
6. hostile or malformed input,
7. deterministic output when relevant.

## Coverage threshold

`npm run coverage` uses Node's native test coverage gate with enforced
thresholds:

```text
lines: 95
branches: 84
functions: 95
```

The primary GitHub Actions check and BIZRA Review Gate run this coverage command
after `npm test` and before `npm run check`.

## Secret-scanning gate (CI)

`.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml` runs gitleaks v8.30.1 on every pull request
and every push to main. Invariants:

- SHA-256-verified binary install (no marketplace-action license dependency)
- SHA-pinned `actions/checkout` reference (matches 100% SHA-pinning canon)
- `gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner --verbose --exit-code 1 --redact`
- Fails the workflow on any finding (`--exit-code 1`)
- Redacts secrets from CI logs (`--redact`) so the workflow output itself
  never becomes the leak surface
- Boundary: read-only audit · no repo write · no external publish

The gate is independent of `check.yml` and `bizra-review.yml` — a secret
finding fails its own workflow without blocking unrelated CI runs.
